//: Firestore indexes for KinetixFSL. Deploy with the Firebase CLI:
//note: These are COLLECTION GROUP single-field indexes. Firestore auto-creates single-field indexes for normal (collection-scoped) queries, but a collectionGroup() query needs the field's index explicitly promoted to collection-group scope — which is what each fieldOverride below does.

indexes.//: Admin Reports & Moderation queue: reports filtered by status and shown newest-first (moderation.js subscribeReports).
Admin Content Validation queue: posts awaiting validation, newest-first (validation.js subscribeValidationQueue).

//progressNote: PHASE 3 — the admin analytics collection-group read over users/{uid}/progress/current (learners.js) needs NO index here: it's a bare collectionGroup('progress') query with no where/orderBy, and Firestore never requires an index for an unfiltered 'return the whole collection group' read. (An earlier attempt to add a `__name__` field override for this failed to deploy — `__name__` is a reserved field path and can't be targeted by a fieldOverride.)

fieldOverrides.//: PHASE 4 — the successor to the `items.fromUserId` override below, for the new nested notifications path users/{uid}/notifications. Lets a user find every notification they've sent so a rename updates old rows (NotificationRepository.propagateSenderName). Deploy and let it build BEFORE shipping the code that queries it, then drop the `items` override in Phase 5.

PHASE 5 REMOVAL — drop this once Phase 4 is verified and the old notifications/{uid}/items collection has drained. Lets a user find every notification they've ever sent, across all recipients' inboxes, so changing their name/photo updates OLD notifications too (NotificationRepository.propagateSenderName). Without this the collection-group query fails and the sync silently no-ops.

Backs the profile 'Comments' tab and the name/avatar propagation onto old comments (CommunityRepository.commentsByAuthor / propagateAuthorName / propagateAvatarUrl). You likely created this already the first time the Comments tab loaded; it's listed here so a fresh project gets it too.

Lets the account-deletion sweep find every vote a departing user cast, across all posts, so it can remove them and correct each post's counts (AccountEraser.deleteOwnVotesEverywhere). Votes carry a userId field for exactly this query.
